lem-ip-distributional-radon-representati:
## Statement

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open. If two finite signed Radon measures on $\Omega$ have the same integrals against every function in $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, then the measures are equal.
lem-ip-vector-radon-variation-is-radon:
## Statement

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $\mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m)$ have finite signed Radon coordinate measures. For Borel $A\subseteq\Omega$ define $$V(A):=\sup\left\{\sum_{j=1}^\infty |\mu(A_j)|:(A_j)_{j\ge1}\text{ is a Borel partition of }A\right\},$$ where the norm is Euclidean. Then $V$ is a finite positive Radon measure and $$V(\Omega)=\sup\left\{\int_\Omega f\cdot d\mu:f\in C_c(\Omega;\mathbb R^m),\ |f(x)|\le1\right\}.$$
lem-ip-open-euclidean-locally-finite-smo:
## Statement

If an open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is covered by a countable family of open sets $(V_\ell)_{\ell\in I}$, then there is a countable locally finite family of nonnegative functions $(\eta_j)\subset C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ summing to one, with each $\operatorname{supp}\eta_j$ contained in one member $V_\ell$ of the cover. Locally finite means that each point has a neighborhood meeting only finitely many supports.
lem-ip-smooth-compact-support-dense-in-c:
## Statement

For every open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, the space $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ is dense in $C_0(\Omega)$ in the uniform norm.
lem-ip-lw-integral-inequality:
## Statement

Let $n\ge2$. For each $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ let $g_i:\mathbb R^{n-1}\to[0,\infty)$ be Lebesgue-measurable and integrable, with its arguments identified with all coordinates except $x_i$. Then $$\int_{\mathbb R^n}\prod_{i=1}^n g_i(x_1,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_n)^{1/(n-1)}\,dx\le\prod_{i=1}^n\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{n-1}}g_i\right)^{1/(n-1)}.$$
lem-ip-bv-zero-gradient-constant-on-conn:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and connected. If $u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ satisfies $\partial_i u=0$ as a distribution for every coordinate $i$, then there is a constant $c\in\mathbb R$ such that $u=c$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$.
lem-ip-l1-sequence-compactness-by-cell-a:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(v_k)$ be a sequence in real $L^1(\mathbb R^n)$, with $\sup_k\|v_k\|_1<\infty$, all zero almost everywhere outside one bounded set. If $\lim_{r\downarrow0}\sup_{k,\ |h|\le r}\|v_k(\cdot+h)-v_k\|_1=0$, then a subsequence converges in $L^1(\mathbb R^n)$. This assertion does not require Dependent Choice.
lem-ip-lipschitz-graph-area-and-calculus:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $m\ge1$, let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $h:Q\to\mathbb R$ be locally Lipschitz. Then $h$ is differentiable almost everywhere, its partial derivatives are measurable and are its weak derivatives. On every open region where $h$ is $L$-Lipschitz, $|Dh|\le L$ almost everywhere. Let $H^m$ denote the repository's unnormalised Hausdorff measure, put $c_m=H^m((0,1]^m)$, and write $\sigma_m=c_m^{-1}H^m$ also on Euclidean spaces containing $m$-dimensional subsets. The graph map $F(y)=(y,h(y))$ satisfies, for every nonnegative Borel $a$,
$$\int_{F(Q)}a(x)\,d\sigma_m(x)=\int_Qa(F(y))\sqrt{1+|Dh(y)|^2}\,dy.$$
For the epigraph $G=\{(y,z):y\in Q,\ z>h(y)\}$, a smooth vector field compactly supported away from the chart sides satisfies
$$\int_G\operatorname{div}\phi\,dx=\int_Q\phi(y,h(y))\cdot(Dh(y),-1)\,dy.$$
Thus its outward normal is $(Dh,-1)/\sqrt{1+|Dh|^2}$ almost everywhere. The sign reverses for a subgraph. The graph surface measure is locally finite and Radon on $F(Q)$ with its relative topology, and its null sets coincide with graph images of Lebesgue-null subsets of the base.
def-ip-spatial-bv-and-distributional-tv:
## Definition

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $u\in L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, where elements of $L^1$ are almost-everywhere equivalence classes. For each $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, its distributional derivative $D_i u$ acts on $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ by
$$\langle D_i u,\varphi\rangle:=-\int_\Omega u\,\partial_i\varphi\,dx.$$
The function $u$ is in $BV(\Omega)$ when each $D_i u$ is represented by a finite signed Radon measure and the resulting vector-valued measure $Du=(D_1u,\ldots,D_nu)$ has finite total variation. Here a finite vector-valued Radon measure means that its partition variation is a finite Radon measure. For a Borel set $A\subseteq\Omega$, define
$$|Du|(A):=\sup\left\{\sum_{j=1}^\infty |Du(A_j)|:\ (A_j)_{j\ge1}\text{ is a Borel partition of }A\right\},$$
using the Euclidean norm on each vector value. Define the spatial total variation by $TV(u;\Omega):=|Du|(\Omega)$. A Lebesgue-measurable set $E\subseteq\Omega$ of finite measure has finite perimeter relative to $\Omega$ when $\chi_E\in BV(\Omega)$; its relative perimeter is $P(E;\Omega):=TV(\chi_E;\Omega)$.
lem-ip-unit-vector-density-has-scalar-va:
## Statement

Let $X$ be a locally compact second-countable metric space, let $\lambda$ be a finite positive Radon measure on $X$, and let $
u:X	o\mathbb R^m$ be continuous with $|
u(x)|=1$ for every $x$. Define the vector measure $\mu(A):=\int_A
u\,d\lambda$ on Borel sets. Its partition variation satisfies $|\mu|=\lambda$.
lem-ip-euclidean-radon-representation-un:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For every open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, every bounded real linear functional on $C_0(U;\mathbb R)$ is integration against a unique finite signed Radon measure. No Dependent Choice assumption is required.
lem-ip-bv-test-field-characterization-an:
## Statement

For every open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and real-valued $u\in BV(\Omega)$, $$TV(u;\Omega)=\sup\left\{\int_\Omega u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi\,dx:\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^n),\ |\varphi(x)|\le1\right\}.$$ If $u_k,u\in BV(\Omega)$ are real-valued and $u_k\to u$ in $L^1(\Omega)$, then $TV(u;\Omega)\le\liminf_kTV(u_k;\Omega)$. In addition, assuming Countable Choice, for any real-valued $u\in L^1(\Omega)$ the displayed supremum is finite if and only if $u\in BV(\Omega)$, with equality to $TV(u;\Omega)$; under the same assumption, an $L^1$ limit of real-valued BV functions with bounded liminf total variation belongs to $BV(\Omega)$ and satisfies the same lower-semicontinuity inequality.
def-ip-boundary-tv-conventions:
## Definition

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, meaning a bounded open set whose boundary has a finite cover by coordinate neighborhoods in which it is the graph of a Lipschitz function and $\Omega$ lies on one side of that graph. For $u\in BV(\Omega)$ define the Neumann total variation by $TV_N(u;\Omega):=|Du|(\Omega)$. Define its zero extension $\widetilde u\in L^1(\mathbb R^n)$ by $\widetilde u=u$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\widetilde u=0$ almost everywhere on $\mathbb R^n\setminus\Omega$. Define the Dirichlet total variation by $TV_D(u;\Omega):=TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^n)$ when $\widetilde u\in BV(\mathbb R^n)$ and by $TV_D(u;\Omega):=+\infty$ otherwise. For $v\in BV(\mathbb R^n)$ define the full-space total variation by $TV_F(v):=TV(v;\mathbb R^n)$. Thus Neumann variation counts only the distributional derivative inside $\Omega$, while Dirichlet variation also counts any jump created by zero extension across $\partial\Omega$.
lem-ip-bv-smooth-coarea:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $u\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\Omega)$ satisfy $\int_\Omega|\nabla u|\,dx<\infty$. For $t>0$ set $E_t^+:=\{x\in\Omega:u(x)>t\}$ and for $t<0$ set $E_t^-:=\{x\in\Omega:u(x)<t\}$. Then the level sets have finite perimeter relative to $\Omega$ for almost every applicable $t$, and
$$\int_\Omega|\nabla u|\,dx=\int_0^\infty P(E_t^+;\Omega)\,dt+\int_{-\infty}^0P(E_t^-;\Omega)\,dt.$$
lem-ip-bv-one-sided-trace-on-lipschitz-g:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. In a Lipschitz graph chart let $G$ be the side $z>h(y)$, and let $u\in BV(G)$ locally, with finite $L^1$ norm and variation on each smaller bounded graph collar under consideration. On every smaller base box $B$ there is a unique local $L^1(B)$ trace $\tau u$ such that
$$u(y,h(y)+t)\longrightarrow\tau u(y)\quad\text{in }L^1(B)\text{ as }t\downarrow0\text{ through almost every }t.$$
The trace is linear and satisfies a bound $\|\tau u\|_{L^1(B)}\le C(a^{-1}\|u\|_{L^1(C_{2a})}+|Du|(C_{2a}))$, where $C_{2a}$ is a fixed larger graph collar with positive margins at the chart sides and $a>0$ is sufficiently small. For every smooth vector field $\phi$ compactly supported away from those sides,
$$\int_Gu\operatorname{div}\phi=-\int_G\phi\cdot dDu+\int \tau u(y)\phi(y,h(y))\cdot(Dh(y),-1)\,dy.$$
The corresponding assertions hold for the subgraph with the normal reversed. For an interval endpoint in dimension one, the same assertions mean the one-sided scalar limit, the usual endpoint sign, and counting measure on the boundary.
lem-ip-bv-strict-approximation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For every open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $u\in BV(\Omega)$ there is a sequence $u_k\in C^\infty(\Omega)$ such that $u_k\to u$ in $L^1(\Omega)$ and $\int_\Omega |\nabla u_k|\,dx\to TV(u;\Omega)$. When $\Omega=\mathbb R^n$, the approximating functions may be chosen compactly supported.
lem-ip-bv-lipschitz-trace-and-zero-exten:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Here $\mathcal H^m$ on a boundary denotes normalized Hausdorff measure: the repository's unnormalised $m$-dimensional Hausdorff measure divided by $c_m=H^m((0,1]^m)$ for $m\ge1$, and counting measure for $m=0$. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, meaning a bounded open set whose boundary has a finite cover by coordinate neighborhoods in which it is the graph of a Lipschitz function and $\Omega$ lies on one side of the graph. There is a unique bounded linear trace operator $T:BV(\Omega)\to L^1(\partial\Omega,\mathcal H^{n-1})$ such that for every $u\in BV(\Omega)$ and $\phi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R^n)$, $$\int_\Omega u\,\operatorname{div}\phi\,dx=-\int_\Omega\phi\cdot dDu+\int_{\partial\Omega}Tu\,\phi\cdot\nu\,d\mathcal H^{n-1},$$ where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal defined almost everywhere on $\partial\Omega$. The zero extension $\widetilde u$ belongs to $BV(\mathbb R^n)$ and satisfies $$TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^n)=TV(u;\Omega)+\|Tu\|_{L^1(\partial\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\bigl(\|u\|_{L^1(\Omega)}+TV(u;\Omega)\bigr)$$ for a finite constant $C_\Omega$ depending only on the domain. The same conclusions hold in dimension one for a bounded open set with a finite one-sided graph cover, with the two one-sided endpoint traces and counting measure on its finite boundary.
lem-ip-bv-coarea-formula:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $u\in BV(\Omega)$, and for $t>0$ set $E_t^+:=\{x\in\Omega:u(x)>t\}$ while for $t<0$ set $E_t^-:=\{x\in\Omega:u(x)<t\}$. Then for almost every applicable $t$ these sets have finite perimeter relative to $\Omega$, and $$TV(u;\Omega)=\int_0^\infty P(E_t^+;\Omega)\,dt+\int_{-\infty}^0P(E_t^-;\Omega)\,dt.$$
lem-ip-bv-sobolev-inequality:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and let $n\ge2$. Every $u\in BV(\mathbb R^n)$ satisfies $$\|u\|_{L^{n/(n-1)}(\mathbb R^n)}\le TV(u;\mathbb R^n).$$
lem-ip-bv-extension-and-translation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, meaning a bounded open set whose boundary has a finite cover by Lipschitz graph neighborhoods with $\Omega$ on one side of each graph. The zero-extension map is bounded from $BV(\Omega)$ to $BV(\mathbb R^n)$, with support in $\overline\Omega$, and there is a finite $C_\Omega$ such that $$\|\widetilde u\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^n)}+TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^n)\le C_\Omega\bigl(\|u\|_{L^1(\Omega)}+TV(u;\Omega)\bigr)$$ for every $u\in BV(\Omega)$. For every $v\in BV(\mathbb R^n)$ and $h\in\mathbb R^n$, $$\|v(\cdot+h)-v\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^n)}\le |h|TV(v;\mathbb R^n).$$
lem-ip-bv-compactness-lower-semicontinui:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, meaning a bounded open set whose boundary has a finite cover by Lipschitz graph neighborhoods with $\Omega$ on one side of each graph. Total variation is lower semicontinuous under $L^1(\Omega)$ convergence of BV functions. Every sequence $(u_k)\subset BV(\Omega)$ satisfying $$\sup_k\bigl(\|u_k\|_{L^1(\Omega)}+TV(u_k;\Omega)\bigr)<\infty$$ has a subsequence converging in $L^1(\Omega)$ to a function in $BV(\Omega)$.
lem-ip-bv-extension-translation-and-coar:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For every bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ (a bounded open set with a finite Lipschitz graph cover of its boundary, with the domain on one side of each graph), zero extension is a bounded map $BV(\Omega)\to BV(\mathbb R^n)$ with support in $\overline\Omega$ and satisfies $\|\widetilde v\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^n)}+TV(\widetilde v;\mathbb R^n)\le C_\Omega(\|v\|_{L^1(\Omega)}+TV(v;\Omega))$; translations satisfy $\|w(\cdot+h)-w\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^n)}\le|h|TV(w;\mathbb R^n)$ for $w\in BV(\mathbb R^n)$; and, for every open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and every $u\in BV(U)$, if $E_t^+:=\{x\in U:u(x)>t\}$ for $t>0$ and $E_t^-:=\{x\in U:u(x)<t\}$ for $t<0$, then these sets have finite perimeter for almost every applicable $t$ and $$TV(u;U)=\int_0^\infty P(E_t^+;U)\,dt+\int_{-\infty}^0P(E_t^-;U)\,dt.$$
lem-ip-finite-perimeter-relative-isoperi:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice, let $n\ge2$, and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz domain (a bounded open set with a finite Lipschitz graph cover of its boundary, with the domain on one side of each graph, and not separable into two disjoint nonempty relatively open subsets). There is a constant $C_\Omega<\infty$ such that every measurable $E\subseteq\Omega$ with $\chi_E\in BV(\Omega)$ satisfies $$\min\{|E|,|\Omega\setminus E|\}^{(n-1)/n}\le C_\Omega P(E;\Omega).$$
